QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_7

question.text: As per SEBI's operational framework for AIF performance benchmarking, which Indian association's membership threshold is used for notifying Benchmarking Agencies, and which three agencies currently publish AIF benchmarks?

answer.text: IVCA, representing at least 33% of AIFs; agencies are CRISIL, NSE and Preqin.
AMFI, representing at least 51% of AIFs; agencies are CRISIL, ICRA and CARE.
APMI, representing at least 25% of AIFs; agencies are Cambridge, Preqin and PitchBook.
SEBI itself directly appoints Value Research, CRISIL and Morningstar.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter 7.6, an association of AIFs representing at least 33% of the number of AIFs may notify one or more Benchmarking Agencies. The Indian Private Equity & Venture Capital Association (IVCA) has done so, and the three benchmarking agencies currently publishing AIF benchmarks are CRISIL, NSE and Preqin. **The Trap:** AMFI is for mutual funds; APMI is for portfolio managers (not AIFs); SEBI sets the framework but does not directly appoint benchmarking agencies. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same SEBI framework across all three AIF categories. XXI-B refers to APMI-notified benchmarks for PMS. XIX-A distributors must cite the IVCA-notified benchmark in marketing material. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** As a Cat I/II Manager, you MUST execute a confidentiality-preserving data-sharing agreement with at least one notified benchmarking agency within 1 year of First Close — non-reporting is a SEBI enforcement trigger.
